categories.why: Start here: what the words mean, what to read first, what you need to know.

categories.title: Get it running

categories.title: Shape
categories.why: The parts, what each does and how they fit together.

categories.title: Execution
categories.why: Where the program starts, how it comes up and what runs at once.

categories.title: Boundaries
categories.why: What goes in and out, what you owe other systems and where you can plug in.

categories.title: Data
categories.why: What the data looks like, where it lives and which copy is true.

categories.title: Behaviour
categories.why: The rules the code enforces and what happens when it goes wrong.

categories.title: Working here
categories.why: How to write a change that fits, and what protects you when you make one.

categories.title: History and change
categories.why: What moves, what moves together, what is half-done and why it is this way.

categories.title: Health and risk
categories.why: Where the repository has drifted: docs, dead code, upgrades.

categories.why: Who owns and knows what, and who to ask.

questions.question: In what order should I read the code, and where do config, tests, build and docs live?
What do the domain terms mean?
What technologies and idioms must I know, and which are probably new to me?
What do I need locally?
How do I build, test, run, release, roll back and deploy?
What do the CI gates guarantee?
What are the main components?
What does each do and how does it work, including cross-cutting concerns?
How do components interact?
Where are the layer boundaries and who breaks them?
What third-party code does each part rely on?
Where is execution entered?
What happens from entry to ready?
What is the concurrency model?
What are all the inputs and outputs?
What contracts do I owe other systems, and who consumes them?
What extension points exist?
What are the data structures and schema?
Where does state live, and who writes and reads it?
What is the source of truth, what is derived, and which stores hold it?
What is the data lifecycle, and where are the sensitive fields?
What are the business rules and invariants?
How does it fail, and how would I notice in production?
How do I write code that fits here?
What are the team's branching, commit and PR conventions?
What do the tests cover, and can I trust a green run?
What breaks if I change X?
What changes most, and what never does?
What changes together without a code link?
What work is in flight?
Which refactors or migrations are half-finished?
Why is it this way? Which decisions and oddities need explaining?
Does the documentation match the code?
Is there dead code, or are there stale flags and unused endpoints?
What is the upgrade burden (end-of-life runtimes, lagging frameworks)?
Who owns and knows what, and what is the bus factor?
What was not analysed, and what could not be resolved?
Where might the extractors be wrong?
How fresh is the dossier relative to HEAD?
How was this dossier produced, step by step, and what did a model do versus a tool?
